prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the dining table directly in front of the camera wearer, extending from within roughly 0.2–0.4 m at the bottom edge to the seated person opposite at about 1.0–1.5 m; the foreground arms, plates and food are among the nearest regions. A partly visible person on the left is approximately 0.5–0.9 m away, while the striped-shirt person behind and to the right of the opposite diner appears farther away, roughly 1.5–2.5 m; the people are separated from one another by about 0.8–1.5 m around the table. The opposite person remains across the table and generally faces the camera wearer, with small forward/backward upper-body shifts across the five frames, while the foreground hands move over the near edge of the table within the camera wearer’s arm’s reach. The map makes near-to-far layering and occlusion by the table easier to see than RGB, including the left person being partly outside the frame and foreground objects hiding parts of the tabletop, but broad similar-gray surfaces, missing detail, and inconsistent boundaries make the metric distances only rough.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates the large dining table in front from several person instances: one centered across the table, one partly cut off at the left edge, and additional people or person fragments near the right and rear; chairs are marked behind or beside the central person. It shows that the central person is roughly 1.0–1.5 m in front of the camera wearer, the left-edge person is closer at roughly 0.5–0.9 m, and the rear/right people and chairs are about 1.5–2.5 m away, although these distances come from RGB context rather than the masks themselves. Across the frames, the central person stays opposite and facing approximately toward the camera, the left person remains strongly cropped, and right-side person fragments enter or leave the visible boundary as the viewpoint shifts; the near tabletop remains within the camera wearer’s reach and also within reach of the central person from the far edge. The instance colors reveal which visible fragments belong to separate people and clarify table/person occlusions better than RGB, but the table mask changes color and shape, small objects such as plates and utensils are largely missing, and several person/chair labels fragment, merge, or appear misplaced.
descriptions.pose: The pose map isolates the seated person opposite the camera wearer, placing the head above the shoulders near the upper center of each frame, the torso behind the far table edge, and the arms extending down and outward toward the tabletop; magenta hand keypoints mark hands near the person’s right side in several frames. The central skeleton remains about 1.0–1.5 m ahead and faces broadly toward the camera wearer, while changes in shoulder, elbow, and wrist positions show modest leaning and arm movement across the five frames rather than a large approach or retreat. The hands lie within the opposite person’s arm’s reach of the food and far half of the table, while the camera wearer’s near tabletop and foreground hands are not reliably represented; other people at the left and rear/right are also absent or only weakly detected. The map makes limb orientation, joint height, and hand position clearer than RGB despite tabletop occlusion, but duplicated head points, unstable or anatomically distorted limb connections, missing lower bodies, and inconsistent hand detections make gaze direction, exact facing angle, and distances unreliable.
